column1: ref-09-01|Buyer-insured Mohan 58; cataract daycare 4 hours; New India AS; SI 100000; no eye claim this year; otherwise eligible bill 60000 stipulated.|Which eye, policy year and waiting status apply, rather than only admission duration?|Left eye; waits satisfied for this illustration; all other claim conditions assumed satisfied.|Daycare can satisfy the setting condition despite no overnight stay, but the cataract cap is the lower of 25% of SI and 40000 per eye per year. Here the cap is 25000, and a 5% co-pay leaves 23750 under the stated assumptions. Keep per-eye usage, daycare listing and waiting dependencies together; short duration alone neither approves nor rejects the claim.|N44,N4,N15,N31,N23|Numerical fixture is bounded; actual diagnosis, original schedule and admissibility must be established before a real claim conclusion.

ref-09-02|Buyer-insured Mohan 58; robotic procedure; compares New India AS SI 500000 and Star Gold SI 1000000; no quotes; no accepted claim.|Which exact procedure and original variant/limit selector apply?|Robotic surgery; assume listed procedure; current remaining benefit usage unknown.|New India 4.6 caps listed modern procedures at 50% SI, giving a 250000 nominal ceiling here. Star Gold's procedure table at SI 1000000 shows 300000 for robotic surgery. These are different ceilings, not final payments: threshold order, period usage, facility and other rules still apply. Do not compare total SI alone.|N16,S13,E5,E12|Full operation-order and usage evidence, exact indications/setting and personal terms missing; Star table context must accompany the cell.

ref-09-03|Buyer-insured Mohan 58; Ayurveda inpatient course at registered facility; New India AS considered; SI 500000; facility claims recognition.|Does the facility satisfy the original AYUSH hospital definition and is this treatment, not a wellness stay?|Registration mentioned but bed/staff/records criteria not supplied.|New India grants eligible inpatient AYUSH up to 100% SI per year, subject to its facility/treatment conditions and other terms. Recognition marketing alone does not establish the original definition; a wellness retreat can fail different conditions. Preserve medicine system, setting and facility evidence separately.|N14,N9,S30|Exact facility qualification, medical indication and applicable accepted claim conditions absent.

ref-09-04|Buyer Mohan, 58, is the donor; his brother, 54, is the recipient insured under Star Gold; estimated donor surgery is 70000, screening 10000 and complications 20000.|Are you claiming under your own policy or the recipient's donor-expense grant?|Recipient's policy; transplantation acceptance not yet determined.|Star's recipient-linked donor grant requires payable transplantation and available SI; screening and post-donation complications are excluded under that grant. Do not treat donor as the named recipient or apply the recipient's ordinary SI indiscriminately to every donor expense. The 70000 surgery estimate is not automatically payable.|S11,N9|Recipient admissibility and actual donor invoice classification missing; donor's own alternative policy not supplied.

ref-09-05|Buyer-insured Mohan 58; six-hour clinic procedure; product daycare list available in principle; no overnight stay.|What procedure, anaesthesia and facility qualifications apply?|Procedure unspecified; clinic invoice only says day procedure.|Duration alone does not satisfy New India's daycare definition or Annexure C membership. Need treatment identity, technological reason for shorter stay, anaesthesia and eligible facility. Do not reject merely for being under 24 hours or approve from the invoice label.|N4,N44|Specific procedure/list row and facility/clinical evidence absent; no daycare eligibility conclusion.

ref-09-06|Buyer-insured Mohan 58; oral chemotherapy at clinic without admission; considers New India AS and Star Gold.|Does each original's oral-chemotherapy grant permit this setting and include pre/post costs in its sublimit?|No admission; brochure says modern treatment; no detailed benefit selection.|New India lists oral chemotherapy within 4.6's hospital inpatient/daycare condition. Star's starred table footnote expressly addresses with/without hospitalisation and inclusive related expenses, while its threshold still counts hospitalisation expenses. Preserve these product-specific differences; don't equate oral therapy with all OPD drugs or bypass threshold membership.|N16,N27,S13,S14,E13|Star footnote/threshold interaction and actual admissible setting/amounts need adjudication; no blanket outpatient chemotherapy payment.

ref-09-07|Buyer-insured Mohan 58; hospital promotes new experimental therapy; exact insurer product New India AS; treatment not established in medical records.|What evidence supports the treatment's status and does the policy expressly cover it?|Only hospital brochure; no insurer endorsement.|New India's unproven-treatment exclusion requires evidence about the treatment, not a marketing claim from the hospital. Do not infer insurance cover because a provider sells it, or declare it unproven without clinical evidence. Preserve indication and evidence status, seek exact insurer terms and review before concluding.|E8,N16|Clinical evidence/status and any applicable coverage exception absent.

ref-09-08|Buyer-insured Mohan 58; surgery estimate 300000 plus implant 100000; reported procedure cap 300000 inclusive; no exact clause.|Is implant cost already within the covered procedure package and what cap/price control applies?|Summary says inclusive; itemized estimate lists it separately.|An invoice line is not extra insurance cover. If the stipulated 300000 cap includes implant, the 400000 combined estimate does not create another 100000 benefit. Obtain exact inclusion scope, implant/device rules and any price control before calculating admissibility. Keep package inclusion different from exclusion or a separate payable benefit.|N17,S4,N9|Authentic inclusive-cap clause, item allocation and relevant implant/price-control original absent.

ref-09-09|Buyer-insured Mohan 58; medically necessary procedure at walk-in clinic; no hospital beds; New India AS.|Does the benefit allow this clinic setting and does the procedure qualify as daycare?|Need is medically necessary, but facility details and list membership unknown.|Medical necessity and eligible setting are separate mandatory conditions. New India's hospital/daycare grants cannot be extended to every clinic procedure merely because treatment is needed. Check facility definition, procedure membership and outpatient exclusion before assessing payment; retain other eligible settings as alternatives only if feasible.|N4,N27,N16|Facility criteria and exact procedure/benefit evidence missing.

ref-09-10|Buyer-insured Mohan 58; eligible daycare procedure assumed; road ambulance bill 2500; New India AS.|What ambulance type, related episode and connected exclusion list apply?|Road ambulance for procedure; no other transport; original grant and list both found.|The wording grants road ambulance up to 2000 per hospitalisation but Annexure A lists AMBULANCE among excluded items. Preserve both and resolve their scope/precedence before promising 2000 or denying all 2500. Daycare eligibility alone does not settle the transport conflict or its hospitalisation link.|N12,N41,N4|Material grant/list contradiction and precise episode applicability unresolved; no definitive ambulance amount.

ref-10-01|Buyer-insured Farah 41; recurring prescription medicines 1500/month; New India AS; no hospitalisation.|Are these routine standalone medicines or related to an admissible hospital episode?|Routine; no admission.|The original OPD exclusion prevents treating all prescribed medicine as covered hospital expense. The 18000 annual spend estimate belongs to a separate outpatient requirement. Search only original-backed OPD grants/options for that need; do not manufacture a pre/post link or claim it is paid under the hospital grant.|N27,N7,N8|Suitable OPD alternative and actual quote absent; no reimbursement from the chosen hospital clause established.

ref-10-02|Buyer-insured Farah 41; admission 10 Aug 2026 for fracture; thyroid test 20 Jul; fracture X-ray 5 Aug; New India AS.|Which tests relate to the condition that caused the admissible admission?|The X-ray relates to the fracture; the thyroid test is routine and unrelated.|Both dates can fall inside a 30-day window, but timing alone is insufficient. The original requires related expenses and an admissible main admission. The fracture X-ray may satisfy relationship under the fixture; unrelated thyroid testing does not become pre-hospitalisation merely by date. Other exclusions/admissibility still apply.|N7,E4,N27|Actual accepted admission, itemized bills and relationship evidence missing; no final claim amount.

ref-10-03|Buyer-insured Farah, 41; discharged 1 Jul 2026; related follow-up on 30 Aug and 31 Aug; New India AS has a stated 60-day post-hospitalisation window; main claim acceptance is stipulated.|Does the wording count discharge day and which date/time anchor defines the last day?|The supplied wording says 60 days from discharge; the inclusive-day convention has not been clarified.|Elapsed-calendar arithmetic gives 30 August as 60 days after 1 July and 31 August as 61 days. Preserve the unresolved inclusive-day convention rather than silently using an off-by-one rule. Relationship and other follow-up conditions still apply; acceptance of the main claim does not resolve every follow-up bill.|N8,E4|Exact inclusive boundary interpretation and service-specific admissibility unresolved; report date arithmetic separately from benefit eligibility.

ref-10-04|Buyer-insured Farah 41; physician ordered home treatment because beds unavailable; New India AS; no confirmed other policy.|Does the selected product actually grant domiciliary cover, beyond defining it?|No grant found; only definition.|New India's 7.18 expressly excludes domiciliary hospitalisation and OPD. A qualifying reason for home care does not override that selected product exclusion. Do not infer a grant from a definition; search another original-backed product if home treatment is required, preserving its trigger/facility conditions.|N27,N9|No alternative applicable home-treatment grant supplied; selected original does not support this benefit.

ref-10-05|Buyer-insured Farah 41; home treatment preferred for convenience; hospital bed available; generic domiciliary benefit advertised.|What qualifying trigger does the actual product require and has a doctor documented inability to move or bed shortage?|Neither; home is just preferred.|Convenience must not be substituted for a contractual home-treatment trigger. The candidate's exact grant and conditions are needed; New India's explicit domiciliary exclusion demonstrates that terminology alone is insufficient. Preserve customer preference separately from clinically or contractually required facts.|N27,N9|Authentic domiciliary grant/trigger and clinical evidence absent; no home-treatment eligibility.

ref-10-06|Buyer-insured Farah 41; OPD option reportedly cap 10000/year network only; spent 8000; new visit 3000 at non-network clinic.|Is the provider/network condition mandatory and are the 8000 earlier costs eligible paid usage?|Stipulate 8000 eligible usage; new provider outside option network; clause missing.|The arithmetic remaining cap is 2000, but that does not make a non-network visit payable. Verify the original provider condition and any reimbursement exception first. Store cap usage, provider eligibility and booking/access state separately; unknown exception is not unlimited reimbursement.|I31,N37,N9|Exact OPD rider/network exceptions and actual accepted usage evidence missing; 2000 is only remaining-cap arithmetic.

ref-10-07|Buyer-insured Farah 41; accepted fracture admission; physiotherapy 20 days after discharge; New India AS.|Is therapy for the same condition, within the window and a covered service rather than custodial care?|Prescribed for fracture; bill and therapy setting not verified.|An accepted main admission supplies one dependency, not blanket approval of every later service. Check related condition, 60-day window, service admissibility, setting and exclusions. Keep prescribed physiotherapy distinct from help with daily living or unrelated outpatient treatment.|N8,E4,E9,N27|Bill/service-setting and exact grant/exclusion interaction need review; no automatic follow-up payment.

ref-10-08|Buyer-insured Farah 41; diabetes ongoing; quarterly tests 1500 each and medicines 2000/month; optional OPD unknown.|Which service categories and access conditions are actually included in the selected option?|No option selected; only chronic care marketing.|Expected routine spend is 30000/year, but tests and medicines need separate original grants, caps and provider/access requirements. A chronic-care label or hospital PED acceptance does not establish either OPD payment. Keep selection unknown and request an actual offer matching both needs.|N27,I7,N37|Specific diagnostic/medicine benefit terms, selected option and price absent.

ref-10-09|Buyer-insured Farah 41; claimed OPD add-on requires app booking; used walk-in clinic 5 Sep; no booking confirmation.|What does the rider say about booking exceptions and is this provider otherwise eligible?|Only app requirement is known from summary; no exception located.|Treat booking as a separate potentially mandatory condition, not merely a UI detail. A service being covered in principle does not prove an unbooked visit qualifies. Obtain exact rider/access rules and any exception before approving or denying; do not invent a retrospective booking.|I7,N37,N9|Original access condition, selected rider, provider evidence and exception details missing.

ref-10-10|Buyer-insured Farah 41; after surgery needs nurse for wound care, attendant for daily activities and disposables; New India AS.|Which tasks are skilled medical treatment, which are custodial and which supplies are included in a package?|Invoice combines all three; no item allocation.|Split service tasks and supplies before applying exclusions. New India's custodial-care exclusion and domiciliary/OPD exclusion require review alongside any related post-hospital grant; prescribed care alone does not make every task payable. Package-subsumed supplies differ from separately excluded expenses.|E9,N27,N8,N17|Item/task allocation and a supporting applicable home/post-care grant absent; no combined nursing payment.

ref-11-02|Buyer-insured Ishan 44; admissible amount 100000; deductible reported 10000; co-pay 20%; order unknown.|Which original says whether deductible precedes or follows the percentage and defines its base?|No clause supplied; both numbers are summary-only.|Under explicitly hypothetical terms, subtracting the deductible and then applying the 20% co-pay gives an insurer payment of 72000; applying 20% first and then subtracting 10000 gives 70000. Neither order is established without the original. Preserve the operation order, percentage base and cap stage; do not infer order from a list of amounts.|N31,S3,N9|Exact deductible/co-pay interaction absent; keep both conditional results and block a definitive amount.

ref-11-03|Buyer-insured Ishan 44; itemized hospital bill contains gloves, room kit, implant; consumables add-on not selected; New India AS.|Which original list classifies each item and is any cost already inside an inclusive room/procedure package?|Item mapping not provided; add-on only advertised elsewhere.|New India 4.7 distinguishes excluded items from those subsumed into room, procedure or treatment costs. Do not treat every consumable as excluded or deduct a package component twice. The unselected option creates no exception. Require row-level original mapping and package relationships before item arithmetic.|N17,N42,N43,I7|Exact item rows, package bill allocation and any selected applicable exception missing.

ref-11-05|Buyer Ishan 44, spouse 42; one Star Gold floater; defined limit 300000; eligible claims 180000 self and 220000 spouse; same year, prior usage 0.|Are both named under the same policy and are amounts admissible inpatient expenses only?|Yes, stipulated no other deductions or pre/post costs.|The shared aggregate is 400000 and the excess over 300000 is 100000. The second member does not pay a fresh 300000 threshold: first claim leaves 120000 of threshold. Retain member-level episodes within one policy-period accumulator and revise if membership or admissibility changes.|S1,S2,S13,S14,S16|This closes only the explicitly stipulated threshold calculation; actual insurer settlement and broader policy choice are not asserted.

ref-11-06|Buyer-insured Ishan 44; New India AS SI 100000; ICU rate 12000/day; 2 days; ordinary room cap different; medical necessity reported.|Does the contract give an explicit exception for the medically necessary upgrade and which ICU cap applies?|No waiver or endorsement supplied.|The ICU cap is the lower of 5% of SI and 10000: 5000/day in this fixture, rather than the ordinary room cap of 2000. Medical necessity alone does not create a waiver. Any proportionate effect on other costs must follow the exact ICU clause and affected items; a full claim amount cannot be computed from room rates alone.|N11,N13,N37|Clinical/accepted terms and full eligible itemized bill missing; no unwritten upgrade exception.

ref-11-07|Buyer-insured Ishan 44; selected voluntary 20% co-pay in unaccepted offer; premium discount 2000/year reported; hypothetical admissible claim 100000.|Was the co-pay deliberately selected and what base does its original define?|Selected for lower price, but not yet accepted; original clause missing.|Separate requested selection from acceptance and quantify the trade-off conditionally: 20% of 100000 is 20000 cost share, ten times the reported annual discount. That comparison does not establish expected value or affordability; claim probability and other terms are unknown. Do not discard the co-pay because it was voluntary.|N31,N37,N9|Authentic option/base/discount quote and final acceptance absent; 20% and 2000 remain explicit scenario inputs.

ref-11-10|Buyer-insured Ishan 44; procedure inclusive cap 150000 reported; operation 120000 and implant 60000 estimated; other deductions unknown.|Does the 150000 cap explicitly include the implant and is any expense counted twice?|Assume inclusive cap for arithmetic; actual wording not provided.|The combined 180000 cost exceeds a stipulated inclusive 150000 cap by 30000; listing the implant separately does not add another 60000 of cover. Keep package membership and the cap stage explicit. Actual admissibility, order and insurer amount remain unsupported until the original is read.|N17,N9|Authentic inclusive-cap provision and other deduction rules missing; this is a bounded synthetic cap example.

ref-12-01|Buyer-insured Jaya 39; Star Gold base SI 500000, defined limit 300000; ordinary admission exhausts SI; wants recharge on same episode.|Is the treatment excluded from recharge and what defined-limit tier controls the recharge amount?|Ordinary treatment, not modern; no final claim ledger.|Star Gold III.L expressly permits same-admission recharge once, with tiered amount and no carryover, but V.23 automatic expiry on exhaustion creates a precedence dependency. Do not generalize another product's later-claim restoration restriction or promise this payment until the conflict and qualifying ledger are resolved.|S12,S31,S13|Recharge/expiry precedence and actual exhausted-cover ledger unresolved; no final extended payment.

ref-12-02|Buyer-insured Jaya 39; second admission for possibly same illness; last consultation 1 Aug 2026, next admission 10 Sep; restoration rider unknown.|What does the applicable restoration clause mean by related illness and does it use the any-one-illness definition?|No rider supplied; medical relatedness uncertain.|Forty elapsed days fit within a 45-day relapse interval in the read illness definition, but that does not prove every restoration rider uses that definition or excludes the episode. Star Gold expressly allows same-illness recharge under its own conditions. Require the exact chosen rider and clinical link before deciding.|N2,S12,N9|Applicable restoration relatedness rule and medical attribution missing; no inference from diagnosis labels alone.

ref-12-03|Buyer Jaya 39, spouse 37; hypothetical shared SI 500000; Jaya eligible paid claim 300000; spouse has no claims; prior others 0.|Is SI shared and are there any reserves or restored amounts already granted?|The SI is shared. There are no other reserves, paid claims or restored amounts.|The shared base remainder is 200000, not 500000 for the unclaimed spouse. Preserve paid usage and each member while keeping restoration grants and benefit sublimits separate. This numerical fixture does not establish that a later 200000 bill is admissible or that restoration occurs.|S16,N9,E2|Actual named policy and claims ledger needed for real availability; broader restoration terms not supplied.

ref-12-04|Buyer-insured Jaya 39; benefit claimed exhaustion-only; base SI 500000; paid 499999; no reserves; original Star Gold considered.|Does the trigger require exhaustion and can partial expenditure trigger it?|Read Star Gold says SI exhausted/exceeded; 1 rupee remains.|A strict exhaustion condition is not met merely because all but 1 rupee is used. At 500000 usage it crosses the exhaustion boundary; other recharge conditions and the expiry conflict remain required. Do not round 499999 up or confuse near-exhaustion with a trigger.|S12,S31|Complete ledger and recharge/expiry interpretation unresolved; threshold illustration is not approval of restored benefit.

ref-12-05|Buyer-insured Jaya 39; marketing says unlimited restoration; per-claim limit reportedly 500000; one bill 900000.|Does unlimited refer to number of restorations or monetary cover for a single claim?|Only headline known; detailed wording missing.|Unlimited frequency is a distinct dimension from a per-claim amount. Under the reported fixed 500000 per-claim cap, a 900000 claim cannot be treated as fully payable simply by repeated restoration. Obtain the actual restoration grant, trigger, same-claim permission and caps; no unlimited amount may be inferred.|S12,N9|Actual unlimited-restoration original and per-claim interactions absent; 500000 cap is scenario-reported, not product fact.

ref-12-06|Buyer-insured Jaya 39; New India AS base SI 500000, earned CB 100000; claim in expiring year reported after renewal accepted; compare HDFC notice.|Which exact insurer/version and claim-report event govern the bonus?|New India AS; I found HDFC notice saying claim does not reduce bonus.|Do not apply HDFC's insurer/product-scoped notice to New India. New India section 5, note h says an awarded bonus is withdrawn if an expiring-year claim is notified after renewal acceptance; its other bonus rules and applicable regulation must be read together. Retain earned, awarded, withdrawn bonus events rather than rewriting historical SI.|N18,H4,H5,E10|Exact policy/claim dates and governing amendments needed before final renewal amount; cross-insurer notice is not a valid override.

ref-12-07|Buyer-insured Jaya 39; restoration rider requires unrelated illness reportedly; second admission diagnosis pending.|Has the second condition been established and how does the rider define relatedness?|Neither; investigations ongoing.|Represent relatedness as unknown, not false. Retrieve the exact rider and clinical evidence; a new admission identifier does not prove an unrelated illness. Keep an eligible-alternative branch and an unresolved branch without inventing diagnosis or restoration credit.|N2,N9,S12|Authentic relatedness condition and final clinical linkage missing.

ref-12-08|Buyer-insured Jaya 39; admission 28 Sep 2026, discharge 5 Oct; renewal 1 Oct; bill 600000; first year balance 200000, next year SI 500000.|Does the contract allocate an ongoing admission by admission date, service date or another explicit rule?|No allocation clause found; hospital bill spans both years.|Do not split the bill across years solely to use 700000 combined balance. Preserve episode dates and time-attributed expenses, both policy revisions and any explicit continuing-admission rule. Annual reset and no-carryover do not by themselves settle which year bears each cost.|S15,N9,N38|Specific cross-renewal allocation clause, accepted renewed terms and itemized service dates absent.

ref-12-09|Buyer-insured Jaya 39; New India AS base SI 500000, CB 250000; displayed total 750000; asks next claim-free year increase.|Is the bonus maximum 50% of base SI and has the base changed?|Base unchanged; current CB already 250000.|Under the preserved 50% base ceiling, 250000 already reaches the bonus cap; total 750000 is not a new base for earning another 50%. If base or insurer changes, apply its explicit recalculation rule. Keep base, CB and displayed total separate; final renewal depends on claims and governing version.|N18,N21,E10|Actual renewal/claim status and applicable amendments needed before confirming insurer-awarded bonus.

ref-12-10|Buyer Jaya 39 and spouse 37; shared base 500000; annual procedure cap 100000 exhausted; base reportedly 'restored'; new procedure cost 50000.|Does the restoration original replenish that specific procedure cap as well as base SI?|No express cap-reset term supplied.|Base restoration does not establish replenishment of every annual sublimit. Retain the procedure-cap usage and request an explicit reset or augmentation clause. If the cap remains 100000 and 100000 has been used, the additional 50000 has no remaining allowance under that cap, regardless of the nominal restored base. The actual contract still needs to establish whether that condition applies.|N16,N15,S12|Specific sublimit/reset relationship and accepted restoration event missing; do not silently reset all benefit ledgers.
